emma_docs: small PR question  i'm rewording the SOC2 retention section to avoid saying 'override' TTLs. legal asked for clearer phrasing around what happens when a hold is applied and then removed. want to show both apply + release examples. thoughts on language and tiny snippets?

lee_security: prefer 'temporarily suspend automated deletion' instead of 'override'. also add a line saying held items continue to count toward storage quotas and backup plans.

prior_auth: legal/compliance: we need to note that release of a hold may reintroduce TTL-based deletion (i.e., the original TTL resumes). suggest phrase: "When a hold is released, normal retention policies resume from that moment."

sam_eng: i'll provide two safe, public-facing examples (curl + ruby). also suggest showing the minimal response for both apply (200) and release (200). use endpoints /v1/audit/holds and include the role names `audit:hold` and `audit:release`.

iris_support: add troubleshooting tip: if a release job fails due to pending litigation flags, customer support will surface the block. also add a link to the audit viewer for customers to verify who applied/released the hold.

emma_docs: draft insertion below. keeping it short and user-friendly.

"Plain language: Applying a legal hold temporarily suspends automated deletion for the specified audit entries. When the hold is released by an authorized person, normal retention rules resume from that time. Held entries remain auditable and remain subject to encryption settings (including customer-managed KMS)."

Examples (public-friendly):

curl: apply a hold
```ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/holds \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"log_id":"l-42","action":"apply","reason":"investigation"}'
```

curl: release a hold
```ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/holds \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"log_id":"l-42","action":"release","reason":"case closed"}'
```

ruby: release example
```
# ruby (net/http)
require 'net/http'
require 'json'
uri = URI('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/holds')
req = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri, 'Content-Type' => 'application/json')
req['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{ENV['RW_API_KEY']}"
req.body = { log_id: 'l-42', action: 'release', reason: 'case closed' }.to_json
res = Net::HTTP.start(uri.hostname, uri.port, use_ssl: true) { |http| http.request(req) }
puts res.code # expected 200
```

Notes: requires `audit:hold` to apply and `audit:release` to release. Held entries pause TTL-based purges but still count toward quotas and backups. When a hold is released, TTLs will apply again from that point. Holds are recorded in the audit trail (actor + timestamp).

lee_security: LGTM. tiny nit: change wording to 'pause automated deletion' to match other docs.

prior_auth: approve after that nit. :thumbsup:
